summary: Tokua Airport serves Kokopo, the capital of East New Britain Province in Papua New Guinea, and operates as the main gateway to the region since replacing the former Rabaul airport, which was rendered unusable by volcanic eruptions in 1994. Located on the Gazelle Peninsula, it provides essential access for travelers visiting the surrounding volcanic landscapes, WWII historical sites, and world-class diving destinations. The airport handles both domestic flights and limited regional connections, serving as a vital link for tourism and local commerce in this tropical island region.
faqs:
Q: How far is Tokua Airport from Kokopo town center?
A: The airport is located approximately 20-25 km southeast of Kokopo, with a typical drive time of around 30-40 minutes depending on road conditions.

Q: Why was Tokua Airport built instead of maintaining the Rabaul airport?
A: The original Rabaul airport was destroyed by volcanic ashfall from Mount Tavurvur's eruptions in 1994, which buried the runway and made it inoperable, prompting the development of Tokua as the replacement facility.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Tokua Airport?
A: Air Niugini and PNG Air are the primary carriers operating domestic flights connecting Tokua to Port Moresby and other major Papua New Guinea destinations.

Q: Are there international flights from Tokua?
A: Tokua primarily handles domestic routes, with most international travelers connecting through Port Moresby's Jacksons International Airport.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared minibuses are available outside the terminal for transfers to Kokopo and surrounding areas, though it is advisable to arrange accommodation pickup in advance. Rental car services are limited, so booking ahead is recommended for those wanting self-drive flexibility. Road conditions in the region can be variable, especially after heavy rain, so allow extra travel time when catching flights.
local_tip: Pack a light jacket or long sleeves, as the terminal can feel cool with air conditioning, and flights occasionally get delayed due to tropical weather patterns—keeping a flexible schedule on arrival and departure days is wise.
